act out: perform an event by pretending to be the people in it
typical: act out a story/scene/scenario. NOT for: a regular acting job.
The children acted out the story of the birth.
We acted out the argument in class.
show your feelings through your behaviour instead of words
typical: act out anger/fear/problems. NOT for: calmly talking about feelings.
The boy acts out his anger at school.
Stress can make teenagers act out.
add up: calculate the total of several numbers
typical: add up numbers/figures/the bill, add sth up. NOT for: subtracting.
I can add up in my head.
She added up the bill twice.
make sense, as a set of facts or numbers (usually negative)
typical: things don't add up, the figures don't add up. NOT for: simple counting.
His story just doesn't add up.
typical: it all adds up, small costs add up. NOT for: one big sum.
Small expenses add up over time.
It all adds up in the end.
agree with: have the same opinion as someone, or think something is right
typical: agree with sb, agree with a decision/idea. NOT for: accepting a plan or offer.
I don't agree with hitting children.
be good for your health (food or climate); usually negative
typical: food doesn't agree with sb. NOT for: opinions.
Spicy food doesn't agree with me.
The hot weather didn't agree with him.
match a word in number or gender (grammar)
typical: a verb agrees with its subject. NOT for: people sharing opinions.
The verb must agree with the subject.
Adjectives agree with the noun in Czech.
answer back: reply rudely to someone you should obey
typical: answer back to a parent/teacher, answer sb back. NOT for: answering a question politely.
Don't answer me back, young man!
She was punished for answering back.
apply for: ask officially for a job, a place on a course or permission, usually by sending in a form or letter
typical: apply for a job/visa/loan/grant/place/permission, apply to sb for sth. NOT for: using something or spreading something on a surface.
She applied for a job at the local library.
You must apply for a work permit before you travel.
arrive at: reach a particular place at the end of a journey
typical: arrive at + a building/station/airport/hotel (arrive in + a city or country). NOT for: arriving at a conclusion (and not with 'to': not 'arrive to').
We arrived at the hotel just after nine.
The train arrives at platform four in ten minutes.
reach a decision, solution or agreement after thinking or talking about it for a long time
typical: arrive at a decision/solution/conclusion/compromise. NOT for: physical arrival at a place.
The committee arrived at a decision after three hours.
They finally arrived at a compromise that suited both sides.
ask around: ask several people for information or help
typical: ask around for a plumber/information. NOT for: asking one person.
I'll ask around and see if anyone knows.
He asked around for a good dentist.
ask for: say that you want or need something
typical: ask for help/advice/a glass of water. NOT for: asking a question.
She asked for a glass of water.
If you need help, just ask for it.
say that you want to speak to someone
typical: ask for sb at the door/the phone. NOT for: asking about someone.
Someone is at the door asking for Dad.
He called and asked for the manager.
behave in a way that is likely to cause problems for you (informal)
typical: be asking for trouble. NOT for: getting what you wanted.
You're asking for trouble if you drive that fast.
ask out: invite someone to go on a date
typical: ask sb out, ask sb out to dinner. NOT for: inviting someone home.
He asked her out to dinner.
She was too shy to ask him out.
